**Short answer:** Take the contract **only if** you can prove that your cost‑to‑serve (including overhead) will be *below* $1,180 PMPM while still meeting or exceeding all HEDIS targets and you have a fully‑fledged risk‑management program in place. If either of those conditions is uncertain, the deal is too risky for a 40‑physician group that has not yet built a mature population‑health platform. Below is a defensible structure that balances clinical operations, legal exposure, and financial viability. Use it as a template when negotiating with the payer or as a checklist if you decide to walk away. --- ## 1. Baseline Financial Snapshot | Item | Calculation | Result | |------|-------------|--------| | **Panel** | 25 000 members | – | | **Capitation rate** | $1,180 PMPM | – | | **Monthly revenue** | 25 000 × $1,180 | **$29.5 M** | | **Annual revenue** | $29.5 M × 12 | **$354 M** | ### What you need to beat - **Average Medicare Advantage cost per member per month (ACPM)** for a typical 65+ panel is roughly **$1,200–$1,400 PMPM** (including hospital, pharmacy, and ancillary services). - If your *actual* cost of care + overhead is **> $1,180 PMPM**, you will lose money even before quality bonuses. - A realistic target: **Cost ≤ $1,100 PMPM** after risk‑adjustment and carve‑outs, leaving a cushion for bonuses. --- ## 2. Clinical Operations – What Must Be in Place | Domain | Key Requirements | Why It Matters | |--------|------------------|----------------| | **Population Health Analytics** | • Real‑time dashboards of risk scores (e.g., CMS Hierarchical Condition Category, HCC).
• Predictive models for high‑cost patients. | Enables proactive care coordination and cost containment. | | **Care Coordination Team** | • 1–2 full‑time care managers per 1 000 members.
• Clinical pharmacists for medication reconciliation.
• Social workers for SDOH interventions. | Reduces avoidable ER visits, readmissions, and pharmacy waste. | | **EHR Integration & Data Exchange** | • Seamless bidirectional data flow with payer’s analytics platform.
• Standardized HL7/FHIR interfaces for claims, lab results, and care plans. | Accurate reporting of HEDIS metrics and risk‑adjusted payments. | | **Quality Management** | • Dedicated quality officer to monitor HEDIS, CMS star ratings, and readmission rates.
• Continuous improvement cycles (Plan–Do–Study–Act). | Drives bonus eligibility and protects against penalties. | | **Patient Engagement** | • Telehealth platform for chronic disease management.
• Mobile app with medication reminders and health education. | Improves adherence, lowers costs, and boosts HEDIS scores. | --- ## 3. Legal & Compliance Safeguards | Issue | Recommended Clause / Practice | Rationale | |-------|------------------------------|-----------| | **HIPAA & Data Security** | • Mutual Non‑Disclosure Agreement (NDA).
• Cybersecurity insurance (minimum $5 M coverage).
• Regular penetration testing. | Protects patient privacy and limits liability for data breaches. | | **Fraud & Abuse** | • Payer’s audit rights with 30‑day notice.
• Indemnification clause covering false claims. | Ensures compliance with the False Claims Act and Medicare Anti‑Kickback Statute. | | **Quality Reporting** | • Clear definition of HEDIS metrics, data sources, and reporting timelines.
• Penalty schedule for underperformance (e.g., 5% reduction in capitation). | Aligns incentives and reduces risk of unexpected penalties. | | **Termination & Exit** | • Early termination for non‑performance or breach with a buy‑out option.
• Minimum term of 3 years, renewable on performance review. | Provides exit strategy if the partnership fails to meet financial or quality goals. | | **Insurance & Liability** | • Professional liability (malpractice) insurance ≥ $10 M per claim.
• General liability and cyber‑risk coverage. | Covers claims arising from clinical care or data handling. | --- ## 4. Financial Viability – Deal Structure ### A. Base Capitation - **Rate:** $1,180 PMPM (fixed). - **Adjustment:** +$200 PMPM for dual‑eligible members; +$150 PMPM for patients with ≥ 3 chronic conditions (risk‑adjusted add‑on). ### B. Quality Bonuses | Metric | Target | Bonus | |--------|--------|-------| | HEDIS Composite Score | ≥ 90th percentile vs national benchmark | 5% of base capitation | | Readmission Rate (30‑day) | ≤ 8% | 3% | | ED Visit Reduction | ≥ 10% from baseline | 2% | | **Total Potential Bonus** | – | **≤ 10% of base** | *Bonuses are paid quarterly and capped at 10% of the base capitation to keep the total upside predictable.* ### C. Carve‑Outs - **Hospital & Specialty Services:** Paid separately by payer (e.g., $X per admission). - **Mental Health & Substance Use:** Separate carve‑out with its own fee schedule. - **Pharmacy:** Managed pharmacy benefit; cost shared 70/30 between group and payer. ### D. Stop‑Loss Insurance - **Trigger:** 25% of total panel costs or $X per member (whichever is lower). - **Coverage:** Reimbursement for losses above the trigger, up to a maximum of 50% of total panel costs. *Stop‑loss protects against catastrophic cost spikes from a few high‑utilization patients.* ### E. Performance‑Based Adjustments | Scenario | Adjustment | |----------|------------| | HEDIS score < 80th percentile for two consecutive quarters | 2% reduction in capitation | | Readmission rate > 12% for three consecutive months | 3% reduction | | Penalties are reversible after corrective action plan is approved. | --- ## 5. Governance & Oversight 1. **Joint Oversight Board** – 4 payer reps, 4 group reps, 2 independent experts (finance, quality). 2. **Monthly Data Review Meetings** – Share dashboards, discuss trends, and approve corrective actions. 3. **Quarterly Audits** – Payer audits claims, coding, and quality data; group provides audit trail. 4. **Annual Performance Review** – Determines renewal, bonus adjustments, and any contract amendments. --- ## 6. Decision Matrix | Criterion | Weight | Score (1–5) | Weighted | |-----------|--------|-------------|----------| | Ability to keep cost ≤ $1,100 PMPM | 30% | 4 | 1.2 | | Existing population‑health platform | 20% | 3 | 0.6 | | Quality bonus upside (10%) | 15% | 5 | 0.75 | | Stop‑loss coverage adequate | 15% | 4 | 0.6 | | Legal & compliance risk manageable | 10% | 2 | 0.2 | | Exit strategy robust | 10% | 3 | 0.3 | | **Total** | 100% | – | **3.85/5** | - **Score ≥ 4:** Take the deal with minimal changes. - **Score 3–4:** Take only if you can invest in analytics, care coordination, and risk‑adjustment. - **Score < 3:** Decline or renegotiate. With a current score of ~3.85, the group is *borderline*—the deal is defensible **only** if you can immediately strengthen your cost‑control and quality infrastructure. --- ## 7. Bottom Line Recommendation | Action | Rationale | |--------|-----------| | **Proceed only after** | • Demonstrated ability to keep costs ≤ $1,100 PMPM.
• Full implementation of the above clinical & analytics stack.
• Stop‑loss insurance in place.
• Clear exit clauses and audit rights. | | **Otherwise** | Decline or negotiate a lower base rate (e.g., $1,050–$1,080 PMPM) with higher quality bonus thresholds to offset risk. | If you can meet those prerequisites, the contract offers a high upside: a predictable revenue stream, strong incentives for quality improvement, and an opportunity to showcase your group’s population‑health capabilities. If not, the financial exposure is likely to outweigh the benefits.
